historical_record.description: The City Planning Commission found, 5-0, the Recreation and Park Department's acquisition of the corner property by bequest, as public open space, consistent with the General Plan (Resolution 14622).

The formal garden by the landscape architect Thomas Church, commissioned in 1957 by Mary Fay Berrigan and Brigadier General Paul D. Berrigan on land in the Fay family since 1869, was completed: two terraces with twin latticed gazebos amid rose parterres and a basket-weave parquet deck; the general added an overlook at the top in 1960 or 1961.
The garden, bequeathed with the house to the city by the Berrigans in 1998, opened to the public as Fay Park after a rehabilitation.
